title: Resolutions by twists on $\mathbf P^1_k$
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal G$ a coherent
$\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-module. Then there is an exact
sequence of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}$-modules

$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal E_2\longrightarrow\mathcal E_1
\longrightarrow\mathcal E_0\longrightarrow\mathcal G\longrightarrow0
$$

in which each $\mathcal E_i$ is a finite direct sum of modules
$\mathcal O(d)$, $d\in\mathbf Z$, with the convention of
[def-sc-p1-standard].
(*Source: the graded Hilbert syzygy theorem – the polynomial
ring $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ has graded global dimension two, so every
finitely generated graded $S$-module has a graded free resolution
of length at most two – combined with the description of coherent
modules on $\operatorname{Proj}S$ as $\widetilde M$ for finitely
generated graded $S$-modules; homological algebra; classical, EGA
II, $\S$2, and Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.5.*)

proof.text: Choose a chart-compatible comparison C from proj_shifted_free_is_twist at degree zero. Both projective-line models are locally Noetherian: the glued line is of finite type over Spec k, and an isomorphism is locally of finite type. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence and finite presentation; finite presentation implies finite type. Apply the locally-Noetherian coherent criterion to the pullback of G, then obtain its finite graded representation M, associated sheaf F, chart data, and isomorphism F ≅ C^*G.

Apply graded syzygy to M and its internal scalar-compatible grading. Retain the three free modules, ranks, integer shifts, homogeneous bases, degree-preserving maps, injectivity, the two range/kernel identities, and surjectivity.

Apply the exact graded-chain sheafification theorem to this chain and the supplied chart data for F. It gives three associated sheaves E_i, their chart data, and an exact chain of inverse pullbacks ending at inverse pullback of F, with monic and epic endpoints.

For each i, apply the homogeneous-basis sheaf identification using the basis of the ith free module and the chart data just obtained. This gives inverse pullback E_i ≅ the finite sum of twists with the syzygy rank and shifts.

Pull back the isomorphism F ≅ C^*G along C^(-1). Compose with Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp, pullbackCongr of C.inv_hom_id, and pullbackId to identify the last term with G. Conjugate the three arrows through all four isomorphisms. Monicity and epicity are preserved by composition with isomorphisms. ComposableArrows.isoMk₃ checks the three commuting squares using hom_inv_id, and ComposableArrows.exact_of_iso transports exactness. Supply the ranks, shifts and these arrows as existential witnesses.
